propositions: Full suite scheduler load causes intermittent false stall classifications on git-fetch dribble tests that pass in isolation due to delayed fixture wake-ups reducing actual throughput below configured rate.
Libcurl correctly aborts transfers during scheduling-induced gaps exceeding the low-speed detection window, making scheduler-delayed Python fixtures unable to produce deterministic negative controls.
Tests incorrectly apply the same artificial 2-second window to both zero-byte stall controls and above-floor negative controls; the production 10-second window must remain unchanged.
Cumulative bytes-owed catch-up alone is insufficient because it cannot recover after libcurl aborts during an uninterrupted scheduling gap.

Solution requires splitting test coverage: deterministic unit test for pacing math, fast 2-second window for zero-byte stall cases, one production-window real Git/libcurl integration test, and removal of redundant dribble timing trials.
